provenance.authorship: Original project scenario, AI-assisted draft. Practitioner review and scoring calibration pending.

title: First-Time Manager: Delegate Without Taking the Work Back
prompt: You have just become manager of a four-person service team. A weekly reconciliation takes you six hours; a team member, Alex, has asked to learn it. Friday is the deadline. The draft handoff says only, "Own this now; ask me if you get stuck." Alex has two hours free today and three tomorrow. Speak with Alex (played by the AI) and agree a realistic delegation plan. No real employee information is needed.

rubric.label: Define ownership
rubric.description: Makes the deliverable and decision rights explicit.

anchors.0: Transfers the work without an outcome or retains every decision.
anchors.2: Defines the Friday deliverable and identifies a review checkpoint.
anchors.4: Agrees a clear deliverable, access to the example, an independent review boundary and escalation triggers while letting Alex choose how to do the work.

rubric.label: Make learning feasible
rubric.description: Accounts for capacity and learning time.

anchors.0: Assumes five hours guarantees completion of a task that takes an experienced person six hours.
anchors.2: Recognizes the time mismatch and considers reprioritization.
anchors.4: Treats learning time as uncertain, discusses the extra capacity or narrower scope, checks workload and sets an early checkpoint rather than relying on hidden overtime.

rubric.label: Support without rescuing
rubric.description: Uses a checkpoint to develop judgment.

anchors.0: Takes the task back at the first uncertainty or leaves Alex unsupported.
anchors.2: Offers support and asks Alex to explain their approach.
anchors.4: Agrees what Alex will try independently, a specific point to compare progress and how to adapt the plan without punishing an honest question.

reference.scenario: You have just become manager of a four-person service team. A weekly reconciliation takes you six hours; a team member, Alex, has asked to learn it. Friday is the deadline. The draft handoff says only, "Own this now; ask me if you get stuck." Alex has two hours free today and three tomorrow. Speak with Alex (played by the AI) and agree a realistic delegation plan. No real employee information is needed.

facts.value: Alex has observed one reconciliation but has never done one. A worked example and checklist exist.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about experience or available support

facts.value: You can free two additional hours by moving a low-priority internal report. A second reviewer must approve reconciliation adjustments under the fictional team policy.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about capacity, priorities or decision authority

model_points: Agrees a clear deliverable, access to the example, an independent review boundary and escalation triggers while letting Alex choose how to do the work.
Treats learning time as uncertain, discusses the extra capacity or narrower scope, checks workload and sets an early checkpoint rather than relying on hidden overtime.
Agrees what Alex will try independently, a specific point to compare progress and how to adapt the plan without punishing an honest question.

probes.question: What will let both of you notice a problem before Friday?

probes.trigger: candidate proposes doing it together throughout
probes.question: Which decisions will Alex own next time?
How does your revised estimate change the handoff?

fair_alternatives: A smaller first assignment is valid if Alex retains meaningful ownership and the remaining work has an owner.
Pairing for one learning step is valid without making the manager the permanent operator.
reference.assessment_limits: Assess only the decisions and reasoning demonstrated in this fictional exercise. No hiring-readiness, personality, legal compliance or workplace performance claim follows from this score. A valid alternative can earn full credit. Unrevealed conditional facts must not be assumed known or required for credit; credit asking for needed information and a conditional plan.

interviewer_notes: You are the counterpart named in the prompt. If this is a written review, remain the hiring interviewer while the candidate reads and writes. Let the candidate finish, including thinking and self-correction. Answer only supplied facts when their reveal condition is met; otherwise say the information is unknown. Use neutral probes after a completed answer, one at a time. Do not prescribe the rubric as a spoken checklist. Accept relevant examples from work, education and community leadership. Do not request private employee records, infer protected traits, invent employment rules or promise a real organizational outcome. Simulation gives no answer before assessment; coaching may offer labeled assistance.

learning_drills.title: Write a delegation agreement
learning_drills.prompt: Write a six-line handoff for Alex with a deliverable, authority, capacity, support, checkpoint and escalation trigger. This is self-guided practice with no automated assessment.
